lines.t: Hi everyone, and welcome to the SpeakLab Podcast. I'm Leyla.
And I'm Sam. Today's topic is growing older. And my dad just retired!
Congratulations to him! What is he doing with his free time?
Salsa classes. Twice a week. He's sixty-six and he dances better than me.
[laugh] He sounds young at heart.
Very. My mum tells him, "Act your age!", but she is secretly proud.
My grandmother is eighty, and this year she learned to make video calls.
Wow. Who taught her?
Aysu! A little girl teaching an eighty-year-old. Two generations apart, laughing together.
I love that. And what does your grandmother teach Aysu?
Patience, recipes, old songs. She has so much wisdom.
In England, many older people live alone or in a care home. Here families seem closer.
Usually, yes. Grandparents often live with the family, or very near.
And Mr Aliyev? He's retired too, isn't he?
For ten years. He says his pension is small, but his garden is big. [chuckle]
And his nard games never end. By the way, I found my first grey hair this week.
Oh no! And wrinkles?
A few, around the eyes. From laughing, I hope. My friends say that at forty you're over the hill.
Nonsense. My grandmother says life starts at forty — and again at eighty.
I like her more every week.
Here's your question for your next SpeakLab call: what do you want to do when you're old — and who is the oldest person you know?
Me? Salsa, like my dad. See you next time!
Bye for now!
